title: Back Rank Mate
description: White has Queen on d8, Black King on g8 with pawns on f7, g7, h7. Black King cannot move. White Queen delivers: 'Qxd8#'. What tactical motif is this?

puzzle_data.question: White has Queen on d8, Black King on g8 with pawns on f7, g7, h7. Black King cannot move. White Queen delivers: 'Qxd8#'. What tactical motif is this?

hint_ladder.gentle: Think of recognized tactical attacking motifs in classical chess theory.
hint_ladder.guided: The term describes the geometric trap or historical sacrificial name.

explanation: The back rank mate occurs when a king is trapped behind a shield of friendly pawns with no escape square.

title: Smothered Mate Pattern
description: White Knight moves to f7, checking the Black King surrounded by friendly pieces with no open flight squares. What is this mate called?

puzzle_data.question: White Knight moves to f7, checking the Black King surrounded by friendly pieces with no open flight squares. What is this mate called?

hint_ladder.gentle: Think of recognized tactical attacking motifs in classical chess theory.
hint_ladder.guided: The term describes the geometric trap or historical sacrificial name.

explanation: A smothered mate occurs when a knight attacks an enemy king that is unable to escape because all adjacent squares are occupied by its own friendly pieces.

title: The Greek Gift Sacrifice
description: White sacrifices a Bishop on h7 (Bxh7+) followed by Ng5+ and Qh5 to launch a decisive attack against the castled black king. What is the traditional name of this sacrificial motif?
